seen_animation: A wide trapezoid sack-shaped body sits on a ground line between grey trees, with the doodle's hat-and-oval head on top. In frames 1-8 the head is tipped down and forward to the left, with the hat brim slanting steeply and its strokes crossing over the face. From frame 9 to frame 12 the head rotates upright and levels, the hat brim becomes horizontal, the face looks left, and a short shoulder/arm stroke extends left from the top of the body. Frames 12-16 hold that upright, left-looking pose with only small changes. The body stays planted in the same place throughout.
seen_film: A person wrapped in a large orange cloak tied with cord sits on snow in front of pine trees, the cloak spreading into a wide triangular mass. In frames 1-6 the head, in a dark hood, is bowed down over the chest. Around frames 7-9 the head lifts and the person looks up and to the left. Frames 9-16 hold the head raised and turned left, with small shifts. The body does not move position.
named_subject: A seated cloaked person in a hat (the doodle's hatted figure) who lifts their bowed head and looks left
evidence: Judged from still frames only, not playback. In e.png frames 1-24 the head is bowed and tilted, matching f.png 1-24 where the hooded head is down. In e.png 25-32 the head rotates up and the hat brim levels in small steps per frame, which matches f.png 25-32 where the head rises. In e.png 33-50 the head is level and faces left while the body is still, matching f.png 33-50. g.png shows the character centre moving in a short, continuous, ordered cluster with no gaps or reversals. The body keeps the same size and position in every frame. The left shoulder stroke grows gradually from frame 27 to frame 32 rather than appearing all at once. The only discontinuity seen is in the scenery: the grey bush at the right base of the tree changes outline between e.png frames 8 and 9 (a.png frames 4 and 5).
primary_gap: In the head-down frames (e.png 1-24) the hat brim, face oval and neck strokes cross over each other into a tangle, so the bowed head reads less clearly as the doodle's hat-on-head than it does once upright.
closes_when: In e.png 1-24 the tilted head shows the hat brim sitting above the face oval with the eyes visible and no strokes crossing through the face, the same arrangement as frames 33-50 but rotated downward.
protect: The timing of the head lift (down through ~24, rising 25-32, held 33-50) that matches the film; the fixed body position and size; the gradual per-frame rotation of the head and the gradual growth of the shoulder stroke; the doodle's hat shape, dot eyes and loose single-stroke line quality; the stable grey scenery.
identity_gap: The head and hat are clearly the doodle's, but the body has been reshaped from the doodle's tall narrow sack with a rounded bottom into a wide trapezoid with a straight base line, and the doodle's neck-to-shoulder strokes are hidden in the head-down frames.
